record.paper_title: Mathematical contributions to the dynamics of the Josephson junctions: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: Given the analogy between superconductive Josephson-junction equations and reaction-diffusion systems such as the FitzHugh-Nagumo model, can Robin boundary value problems be formulated and analyzed so as to obtain results relevant to biological phenomena? In this setting, the biological reaction-diffusion side includes a membrane potential u(x,t) and a recovery variable v(x,t) modeling transmembrane current, while the superconductive side is represented by third-order parabolic equations used to describe Josephson-junction phase dynamics.

evidence.quote: Then, an equivalence between the third order equation (2.10), typical of Josephson junctions, and biological phenomena has been pointed out in [29]. Indeed, let us consider the FitzHugh-Nagumo system (FHN): [30, 31]

where u(x, t) represents a membrane potential of a nerve axon at distance x and time t, and v(x, t) is a recovery variable that models the transmembrane current. This reaction-diffusion model characterizes the theory of the propagation of nerve impulses, and the connection between a third order equation like (2.10) and the (FHN) system can be realized changing the first one into the second one under continuous parameter variations [29].

Moreover, according to the analogy between superconductor equations and reaction-diffusion models, the Robin boundary problem would be considered in order to achieve results for many biological phenomena, too [53, 54].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the third-order parabolic equation modeling phase dynamics in a Josephson junction,
  ε(φ_t − φ_xxt) − φ_xx + γ sin φ + α φ_t = f(x,t),   (x,t) ∈ (0,L) × (0,T),
where ε, α, γ > 0 and φ(x,t) denotes the phase difference of the macroscopic wave functions across the junction. Consider also the FitzHugh–Nagumo reaction–diffusion system
  u_t = D u_xx + u(u − a)(1 − u) − v + I(x,t),
  v_t = b u − c v,   (x,t) ∈ (0,L) × (0,T),
with 0 < a < 1, b, c, D > 0, where u(x,t) represents the membrane potential of a nerve axon at position x and time t and v(x,t) is a recovery variable modeling the transmembrane current.

Formulate Robin boundary value problems for both systems, namely conditions of the form
  α₁ φ(0,t) + β₁ φ_x(0,t) = g₁(t),   α₂ φ(L,t) + β₂ φ_x(L,t) = g₂(t),
and analogous Robin conditions on (u, v), with prescribed initial data, and develop a unified analytic theory (existence, uniqueness, regularity, a priori estimates, asymptotic behavior, and dependence on parameters) that exploits the equivalence under continuous parameter variations between the third-order Josephson equation and the FitzHugh–Nagumo system, in order to derive results applicable to the propagation of nerve impulses and related biological phenomena.
artifact.category_tag: Robin problems for third-order parabolic and reaction-diffusion equations
artifact.status_search_result: There are partial results addressing the components of this program: existence/uniqueness theorems for third-order dissipative Josephson-type equations under various boundary conditions, finite element analyses of FitzHugh–Nagumo reaction–diffusion systems with Robin boundary conditions, and works simulating FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron activity via Josephson-junction models. However, no single unified analytic theory linking Robin boundary value problems for both systems with biological applications appears to have been completed, so the broader problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Existence and uniqueness of solutions of a class of 3rd order dissipative problems with various boundary conditions describing the Josephson effect
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes existence/uniqueness for third-order dissipative Josephson-type equations under various boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for third-order Josephson equations with general boundary conditions.

status_evidence.title: Finite element analysis of nonlinear reaction–diffusion system of FitzHugh–Nagumo type with Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Finite element analysis for FitzHugh–Nagumo reaction-diffusion with Robin boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Robin BVPs for FitzHugh–Nagumo have been studied numerically.

status_evidence.title: Simulating the electric activity of FitzHugh–Nagumo neuron by using Josephson junction model
status_evidence.snippet: RCLSJ Josephson model can reproduce FitzHugh–Nagumo dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: The dynamical equivalence between Josephson-junction models and FitzHugh–Nagumo neurons has been demonstrated.
